pattern.crimePattern: passed-over employee poisons the new manager with farm insecticide
pattern.notes: Fictional farm and fictional chemical brand ("Rosetox"). The poison is named only by class (organophosphate); no quantity, preparation or dose is given beyond the stock count the deduction needs.

ob.text: Lakeview Roses, an export rose farm on the south shore of Lake Naivasha, reports that its new farm manager, Caroline Jerop (41), collapsed in greenhouse 7 at 12:10 after drinking tea from her flask, and died before the ambulance arrived.

people.name: Caroline Jerop
people.occupation: Farm manager, Lakeview Roses (two weeks in the post)
people.bio: Came from a farm in Kericho two weeks ago. Brought her own green thermos everywhere.

facts.text: Caroline Jerop collapsed in greenhouse 7 at 12:10 after drinking tea from her flask, and died before the ambulance came.
Caroline collapsed between the rose beds in greenhouse 7. No injuries were seen. Her thermos was beside her.
Her green thermos is half full of tea. The farm medic kept it aside.
On the store door: 'Chemicals handled by trained sprayers only.' Packhouse staff are never trained or allowed.
Stock card, Rosetox bottle #14: opened last month at 500 ml; 420 ml at today's 13:00 count.
Spray log: no Rosetox spraying recorded since bottle #14 was opened. 500 − 420 = 80 ml unaccounted for.
Spray log: today 09:30–11:30, fungicide in greenhouse 12 at the far end of the farm, H. Shitandi with K. Wekesa.
Kevin: he carried the tank behind Hesbon in greenhouse 12 from 09:30 to 11:30. Hesbon never left.
Bottle #14 carries two sets of fingerprints on its shoulder.
Guard's log: '07:30 — chemical store door OPEN, nobody present.'
Guard's log: Daudi's rounds, gate to lake, every half hour from 08:00 to 14:00.
Canteen receipt: H. Shitandi, tea and mandazi, 07:22. The canteen lady says he sat until about 07:45.
Tabitha: at 10:15 Wambui came to the urn and said, "Let me fill the new madam's flask myself, as a welcome."
Tabitha: in twenty years Wambui never filled anyone's flask. "They didn't even eat together."
Notice: 'Congratulations to Caroline Jerop, Farm Manager.' Underneath, scrawled in pen: '20 YEARS'.
Fumigation schedule: greenhouse 7 was last fumigated eight days ago.
Export ledger: stems reconcile to the stem for the month. Nothing is missing.
Labour hearing minutes, Naivasha: S. Kariithi present 09:00–13:00.
Prints given voluntarily for comparison: Hesbon Shitandi and Tabitha Wangui.
Fingerprints taken from Wambui Nderitu in detention.
Autopsy: no injuries. Pinpoint pupils and fluid on the lungs, consistent with organophosphate poisoning.
Autopsy: no blow, no sting, no allergic reaction.
Autopsy: swallowed about 30–60 minutes before she collapsed at 12:10.
Toxicology: an organophosphate, the same compound as Rosetox, in her stomach and in the thermos tea.
Lab: one set on bottle #14 is Hesbon's, as expected. The other matches Wambui Nderitu. Tabitha's prints are not on it.
Hesbon: "The store was locked all day. The key never left my belt."
Hesbon admits he left the store unlocked while he went for breakfast, from about 07:20 to 07:45.
Wambui: "I have never been inside the chemical store."
Wambui: "I was happy for her. I trained her myself."
Wambui admits she went into the store at about half past seven, "for gloves". The packhouse keeps its own gloves.
Samuel: "I was at the labour office all morning."
Samuel: Wambui trained Caroline when she joined. "Then Caroline got the job."

interrogations.intro: Hesbon keeps one hand over the key on his belt. "I'm a trained sprayer. I follow the rules."

topics.reply: Fourteen? I haven't sprayed Rosetox this month. Take my prints. Take them.

interrogations.intro: Wambui sits very straight on a packing crate. "Twenty years I have been here. I trained that girl myself."

topics.reply: Somebody wrote on the notice. Not me. People are angry for me.
I filled her flask as a welcome. Is that a crime now?
I will not give fingerprints like a thief. I have a lawyer's number.

interrogations.intro: Samuel takes the call outside the labour office. "Nine years I ran that farm. Now they call me?"

topics.reply: She trained Caroline. Then Caroline got the job. You understand?

interrogations.intro: Tabitha keeps wiping a clean cup. "I make the tea. Everybody's cup, twenty years."

topics.reply: In twenty years she never filled anybody's flask. Not one. They didn't even eat together.
That boy eats breakfast every morning at seven-twenty. Like a clock.

interrogations.intro: Daudi holds his patrol log open at the morning page. "I write what I see. Every round."

topics.reply: The store door was open at half past seven and nobody inside. I wrote it. I thought the sprayer was coming back.
The boy with the tank. He follows Hesbon all day.

contradictions.reaction: I left it open when I went for breakfast. Twenty minutes. Everybody does. If the farm finds out, I'm finished. Please.
Her hands go still on her knees. "...I went in for gloves. Only gloves. At half past seven." The packhouse keeps its own gloves.

prosecutor.pass: Her prints on a bottle she's never allowed to touch, and her hands on the flask at 10:15. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. The sprayer lied about a door, not a death. Whose hands filled that flask?
No. Count the bottle, then read who stood at the urn at a quarter past ten.

prosecutor.pass: Organophosphate, in her tea. The pathologist and the lab agree.
fail: A hot greenhouse doesn't put insecticide in a thermos. Read the autopsy again.
Fumigation was eight days ago. Try again.

prosecutor.pass: Twenty years, written on a notice board. That's the reason.
fail: That grudge belongs to a man who was at the labour office. Not her reason.
The ledger reconciles. Look at the notice board instead.

timeOfDeath.note: The act window: the poison went into the flask at the tea urn. Death followed at 12:10.

proof.concludes: 80 ml of organophosphate is missing from bottle #14, and the store stood open and unattended while the sprayer ate breakfast. Only trained sprayers may handle it.
The poison was in Caroline's thermos, and the thermos was filled at 10:15 by Wambui, who had never filled anyone's flask in twenty years.

Wambui's prints are on bottle #14 though packhouse staff never touch chemicals, and she lied about going in. Wambui Nderitu poisoned Caroline with organophosphate insecticide in her flask, because Caroline got the post she had waited twenty years for.

eliminations.why: Samuel was at the Naivasha labour hearing from 09:00 to 13:00.
Hesbon was spraying greenhouse 12, at the far end of the farm, with his assistant from 09:30 to 11:30. His lie hid a careless habit.
Tabitha filled every flask for twenty years, and her prints are not on the bottle; Wambui filled this one.
Daudi was walking his logged rounds, gate to lake, every half hour.
The tea in her flask and her stomach both carry organophosphate.
Greenhouse 7 was last fumigated eight days ago.
No sting and no allergic reaction.
The export ledger reconciles to the stem.
The open store was Hesbon's failing, not a reason for Wambui to kill.
That grudge is Samuel's, and Samuel was at the labour office.
There was no money between them; they didn't even eat together.

reconstruction.text: Two weeks ago the owners make Caroline farm manager. Under the notice, someone writes "20 YEARS".
07:20. Hesbon goes to breakfast and leaves the chemical store unlocked, as he always does. At 07:30 the guard writes it down.
Wambui slips in and pours from bottle #14 into a small water bottle. She leaves her prints on its shoulder.
10:15. At the tea urn: "Let me fill the new madam's flask myself, as a welcome."
At about 11:30, in greenhouse 7, Caroline pours her tea.

clockPlan.note: Detain Wambui once Tabitha has spoken; prints take 6 h; press inside the 24 hours. Toxicology (18 h) only adds a line to the verdict.

ui.beatNotes: Counting as evidence: the stock card does arithmetic in the notebook (500 − 0 sprayed = 500 expected; 420 found; 80 missing). Simple maths becomes a deduction the player can see.
